newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip declines.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip declines.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Wednesday due to dips in three highly capitalised blue chips, brokers said.
The all share index closed 5.36 points down at 857.14. Blue chips Aitken Spence & Co fell 34.75 rupees to 190.25, John Keells Holdings 4.75 to 375, National Devlopment Bank (NDB) 10 to 290.
"The declines were probably due to profit-taking, since all three shares had gained sharply in the last month," said a trader at brokerge John Keells.
Turnover was 81.38 million rupees, led by 90,000 shares of NDB.
Foreign buying was worth 17.1 million rupees and selling was 35.7 million.
"Turnover was relatively low, as some buyers were on the sidelines to see if the index would soften if they kept out," said Manjula Kumarasinghe of brokerage Jardine Fleming.

"But given the positive nature of Tuesday's telecom deal with NTT and news on the NDB convertible debenture that should come soon, there isn't much point in buyers waiting on the sidelines," he added.
The government sold 35 percent of state-owned Sri Lanka Telecom to Japan's NTT, for $225 million. It is also selling 22.5 million convertible debentures in NDB.
